ov: The common pheasant is a game bird native to Asia and the far south-east of Europe, and one of the world’s most hunted birds, introduced widely and bred on game farms. Males are brightly coloured, and many have a white neck ring.

why.et: Pheasants are a popular game bird, introduced to many countries to be shot by hunters.

rg: Native to Asia and the Caucasus foothills; introduced widely in Europe and elsewhere.
df: Fruit, seeds, grain, berries and leaves, plus slugs, earthworms, caterpillars, grasshoppers and other invertebrates.
fx: It usually cruises at 43–61 km/h, but can reach 90 km/h when chased.
Its scientific name, colchicus, comes from Colchis, in modern Georgia, where Europeans first came to know the bird.
